newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic's coalition ahead in early poll results.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic's coalition ahead in early poll results.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling leftist coalition was cruising to election victory on Monday, winning popular endorsement for his new peace-making policies despite a troubled economy.

"It is not a question whether we are going to win. It is rather the question of how resounding our victory will be," Slobodan Cerovic, a leading member of the influential coalition partner Yugoslav United Left (JUL), told Reuters.
Cerovic was speaking after initial results of Yugoslavia's first elections since the end of a four-year Balkan war began trickling in and showed Milosevic would lead his coalition to victory.
JUL headed by Milosevic's wife Mirjana Markovic forms the leftist coalition with New Democracy and Milosevic's Socialist Party SPS.

According to initial results from the federal and municipal elections, announced by SPS spokesman Ivica Dacic, the left was winning in nearly all the major towns in Serbia proper and its Vojvodina and Kosovo provinces.

Out of some 240,000 votes counted late on Sunday, it had won twice the amount of ballots cast for the opposition coalition Zajedno (Together) and the third major contestant, the ultra-nationalist Serbian Radical Party (SRS).
Opposition leaders privately admitted defeat.
"I would be ecstatic if we were to get 40 percent of the votes," one told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
Opposition leaders blamed the state-run media, ethnic Albanians, lack of interest by the West and lethargy by voters for their poor performance.

A low voter turnout of 61 percent, reported by the federal election commission, was bad news for the opposition as Milosevic's coalition parties rely on loyal followers -- many of them pensioners -- with disciplined voting habits.
Ironically, Milosevic had already been helped by his foes.

The ethnic Albanian majority in Kosovo and its fringe areas, which account for 15 of the 108 seats Serbia has in the 138-seat federal parliament, helped his candidates to romp home by boycotting the polls.

"They gave him a 15-0 head start over us. Its just like (Kosovo Albanian leader Ibrahim) Rugova joined a coalition with Milosevic," said Milan Bozic, political adviser to Vuk Draskovic, leader of the biggest opposition party SPO.

A team of election observers from the United States and several other states from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) monitored voting at some of the 10,000 polling stations.
But a SPO spokesman criticised the observers. "They came too few and too late. They should not have come at all," he said.
During the campaign opposition leaders were virtually shut out from the state media and were only able to reach voters through rallies and a handful of independent papers.

"Had the West wanted really to help us, was really interested in promoting democracy in Serbia, it would have pressed Milosevic to give us just one independent channel on state television," said Milorad Jovanovic, spokesman of a Zajedno member, the DSS.
The low turnout testified to the widespread apathy among the population. Almost a third now lives in poverty, according to a Red Cross survey.
A year of peace and the end of a U.N. trade embargo has failed to bring economic relief to a country which once enjoyed the highest standard of living in Eastern Europe.
The elections were the first major test for Milosevic's new peace-making policies, highlighted as the leading achievement by the ruling coalition to cover up a bad economic situation.

Although Milosevic was not a candidate in the polls, an election victory for his parties should enable him to push through constitutional change enabling him to stay in power after his second and final term as president expires next year.
Diplomats say he will probably assume the post of federal president after the next federal parliament invests the ceremonial post with strong executive authority.
Official election results were not due before Thursday but unofficial returns early in the week are likely to indicate the outcome.
